title: Find Peak Element
statement: A peak is an element strictly greater than its neighbors. The ends have one neighbor, and the array is treated as bordered by negative infinity. `nums` may contain several peaks. Return the index of any peak.
hints: A linear scan finds a peak by walking uphill.
Binary search also works. If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], a peak exists on the right, because the slope is rising and the border is negative infinity.
Otherwise a peak exists at mid or on the left.

approaches.name: Linear scan
approaches.explanation: Return the first descent, or the last index.

editorial: The negative-infinity borders guarantee a peak. On a rising slope, the peak cannot be to the left of the higher neighbor, so discard the left half including mid. On a falling slope, mid itself may be the peak, so keep it by setting hi = mid. The loop ends on a peak index.

examples.explanation: Either peak is acceptable. The binary search picks one.
